newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-Sweden to cut rates 50 points this week.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Sweden to cut rates 50 points this week.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, was expected to lower its deposit and lending rates by 50 basis points at its board meeting on Thursday to give way for more repo rate cuts, a Reuters poll found on Monday.
Out of 17 economists questioned, 12 believed the central bank would lower its interest rate corridor by 50 basis points.
The corridor is marked out by the deposit rate and the lending rate that currently stand at 4.25 percent and 5.75 percent respectively after being last cut on October 24.
One of the economists forecast a 25 basis points cut and four said there would be no change.
The Riksbank does not have another board meeting until December 19.
The repo rate, the central rate of a three tier system, currently stands at 4.35 percent after being trimmed by 25 basis points last Tuesday, the 24th cut so far this year.
Asked when the Riksbank would next lower the repo rate, 12 analysts forecast another lowering on December 17 after the bank released its fourth and final inflation report for the year.

"Then we have both the Riksbank's inflation report, KI's (The Swedish National Economic Research Institute) report on the economy, Gross Domestic Product for the third quarter and the consumer price index for November," said one economist.
The bank has already said that the repo operation set on December 17 would last for three weeks.
Economists expected the repo rate to be lowered by 10 basis points. It started the year at 8.91 percent.
One economist expected the Riksbank to lower its repo rate on December 10.
None of the economists questioned expected the Riksbank to make any moves on the repo rate at Tuesday's weekly operation at 0830 GMT.
The majority of economists estimated the repo rate would bottom at 4.0 percent in the first quarter of 1997.
Two saw the repo being cut to as low as 3.80 percent.

Analysts interviewed for the poll were from Aragon, Carnegie, Chase, Consensus, Den Danske, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Hagstromer & Qviberg, Handelsbanken, HSBC Midland, Lehman Brothers, Nordbanken, PaineWebber, S-E-Banken, Sparbanken, Transferator, Union Bank of Switzerland, Ohman Fondkommission.
